subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should the shared auth-profile OAuth refresh path retry transient provider/plugin refresh failures by default, and what classifier and retry budget should define that policy?
rationale: The missing retry is source-proven, but auth refresh retry changes failure timing and can mask terminal credential problems or interact with provider-owned refresh hooks, so maintainer intent is needed before encoding policy.

options.title: Approve bounded shared retry
options.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient-error classifier, small retry budget, and tests for success-after-retry, exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

options.title: Keep retries provider-owned
options.body: Leave the shared manager single-shot and require providers/plugins with known transient refresh behavior to implement their own refreshOAuth retry policy.

options.title: Defer for live provider proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers want live upstream transient-failure proof before selecting a generic retry policy.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded shared retry
recommendation.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient-error classifier, small retry budget, and tests for success-after-retry, exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the current OAuth lifecycle manager where the shared retry policy would most likely live.
